title: Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning - CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning - Specialized Requirements
subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: In a traditional Design-Bid-Build (DBB) construction delivery method, who holds the risk if the architectural design contains flaws that require change orders during construction?
options: The construction contractor.
The owner (the public agency).
The bonding surety.
The subcontractor.
questions.explain: In DBB, the owner contracts separately with the designer and the builder. Because the owner supplies the design to the builder (the Spearin Doctrine), the owner warrants the adequacy of the design and bears the risk for design flaws.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A major advantage of using the Design-Build (DB) project delivery method for a new recreation center is:
options: The agency holds separate contracts with the architect and the builder.
It provides a single point of responsibility for both design and construction, and often allows for a faster schedule.
It is the only method that guarantees no change orders will ever occur.
It requires the least amount of technical oversight by the agency.
questions.explain: In Design-Build, the owner contracts with a single entity that provides both design and construction services. This transfers the design-constructability risk to the vendor and allows construction to begin before design is fully complete.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: In the Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) delivery method, the Construction Manager typically guarantees:
options: To finance the entire project on behalf of the agency.
A Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for the construction of the project.
To completely eliminate the need for an architect.
To perform 100% of the construction work with their own forces.
questions.explain: CMAR involves a construction manager who acts as a consultant during the design phase and then acts as a general contractor during construction, committing to deliver the project within a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: When drafting specifications for a Software as a Service (SaaS) procurement, one of the most critical specialized clauses a buyer must include is:
options: FOB Destination shipping terms.
Prevailing wage requirements.
Data ownership, transition, and security requirements.
A physical building blueprint.
questions.explain: Because SaaS applications store the agency's data on the vendor's servers in the cloud, terms explicitly addressing who owns the data, how it is secured, and how it is retrieved upon termination are paramount.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: In IT procurements, a Service Level Agreement (SLA) is utilized to:
options: Determine the initial purchase price of the hardware.
Define measurable performance metrics, such as system uptime and incident response times, and state the remedies for failure.
Dictate the coding language the developer must use.
Establish the terms for real estate leasing.
questions.explain: An SLA forms part of the contract and specifically guarantees minimum acceptable performance metrics (like 99.9% uptime) and provides for penalties or credits if those metrics are not met.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Why might a buyer require a 'Source Code Escrow' agreement when purchasing custom, critical software?
options: To protect the agency in case the software vendor goes out of business, ensuring access to the code necessary to maintain the system.
To ensure the software runs faster on agency servers.
To bypass cyber security reviews.
To allow the agency to resell the software for profit.
questions.explain: Source code escrow places the fundamental code with a neutral third party. If the developer goes bankrupt or fails to support the product, the code is released to the agency so they are not left with dead software.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: An agency wants to contract for software development using an 'Agile' methodology rather than traditional 'Waterfall.' This means the solicitation must be structured to accommodate:
options: A completely defined end-product fully documented prior to bid.
Iterative, incremental development cycles (sprints) with continuous end-user feedback and evolving requirements.
A strict firm-fixed-price for the entire unknown project.
No involvement from agency staff until the very end.
questions.explain: Agile software development is iterative and collaborative. Unlike Waterfall, which requires full requirements upfront, Agile adapts to changes. Procurement contracts must handle phased deliverables and flexible scopes (often via capacity or T&M models with caps).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: When procuring human and social services (such as mental health counseling), which regulatory compliance issue is consistently one of the highest priorities to address in the RFP?
options: The Davis-Bacon Act.
Client data confidentiality and HIPAA regulations.
Building structural codes.
LEED certification standards.
questions.explain: Human services often involve the exchange of sensitive, protected health and personal data. Ensuring the provider complies with HIPAA and maintains strict confidentiality is a critical contract requirement.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A jurisdiction adopts 'Performance-Based Contracting' for a job training social service. The contract payment terms should be based on:
options: The number of hours the trainer spends in the office.
The amount of training material printed.
Measured outcomes, such as the percentage of participants who successfully secure employment.
A flat monthly rate regardless of attendance or success.
questions.explain: Performance-based contracting ties payment to the achievement of specific, measurable outcomes or results, rather than just reimbursing the inputs or effort expended by the contractor.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Before awarding a contract for industrial cleaning chemicals, the buyer must ensure the vendor provides a document outlining chemical handling, storage, and emergency protocols. This document is called a:
options: Material Specification List.
Safety Data Sheet (SDS).
Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest.
Bill of Lading.
questions.explain: Under OSHA standards, Safety Data Sheets (SDS, formerly MSDS) must be provided by chemical suppliers. They detail physical and chemical hazards, toxicity, handling procedures, and emergency response instructions.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), when an agency contracts for the disposal of hazardous waste, the agency retains liability for that waste:
options: Until the truck leaves the agency's property.
Only if the contractor goes bankrupt.
From 'cradle to grave' (meaning forever), even after it is handled by the contractor.
Until the vendor sends the final invoice.
questions.explain: RCRA imposes strict 'cradle-to-grave' liability on the generator of hazardous waste. The agency remains legally and financially responsible for the waste from its creation through its ultimate, final disposal.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: When drafting a Statement of Work (SOW) for complex professional consulting services, the most effective approach is to draft it based on:
options: Specific, measurable deliverables and milestones.
Detailed dictation of the consultant's daily schedule.
Strict hourly tracking rather than end products.
Generic terms that give the consultant maximum freedom to define the project.
questions.explain: A deliverable-based SOW ties payments to the successful submission and acceptance of defined work products (milestones or reports). This ensures the agency pays for actual results, not just hours billed.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: If a public procurement is funded fully or partially by federal grants, the buyer must ensure the solicitation complies with the federal requirements found in:
options: The Uniform Commercial Code (UCC).
The Davis-Bacon Act exclusively.
2 CFR 200 (The Uniform Guidance).
The state's general accounting statutes only.
questions.explain: 2 CFR 200, known as the Uniform Guidance, outlines the uniform administrative requirements, cost principles, and audit requirements for federal awards. Grantees must follow its specific procurement standards (e.g., flow-down clauses).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: The Davis-Bacon Act requires contractors and subcontractors performing on federally funded or assisted contracts over $2,000 for public buildings or public works to:
options: Only hire local unionized labor.
Pay their laborers and mechanics no less than the locally prevailing wages and fringe benefits.
Source 100% of their construction materials from the United States.
Finish construction within one calendar year.
questions.explain: The Davis-Bacon Act protects local wage rates by requiring contractors to pay workers the locally prevailing wages, as determined by the Department of Labor, on federally funded construction projects.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: When purchasing commercial printing services (e.g., thousands of brochures), it is standard industry trade practice to:
options: Require delivery of the exact count to the single digit.
Allow for an overrun or underrun margin, typically up to 10%, to account for press spoilage.
Demand the original press plates be destroyed in front of a buyer.
Pay the printer upfront before the ink is set.
questions.explain: Printing trade customs acknowledge that web and sheet presses generate spoilage during setup. It is standard practice to allow a tolerance for overruns/underruns (often up to 10%) and to bill accordingly based on actual output.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: An agency is transitioning its municipal fleet to alternative fuels. During pre-solicitation, which specialized consideration must the buyer coordinate alongside the vehicle purchase?
options: Changing the uniform colors of the drivers.
Ensuring the necessary fueling infrastructure (e.g., EV charging stations or CNG pumps) exists or is concurrently procured.
Lobbying the state legislature to waive licensing fees.
Requiring all drivers to obtain an IT degree.
questions.explain: Purchasing alternative fuel vehicles without the supportive infrastructure to charge or fuel them leads to operational failure. Infrastructure planning is a critical integrated requirement in alt-fuel fleet procurements.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: To mitigate risk when contracting for an enterprise cloud database that will hold citizen Social Security Numbers, the buyer must ensure the vendor holds what specific type of insurance?
options: Builder's Risk Insurance.
Inland Marine Insurance.
Cyber Liability and Data Breach Insurance.
Automobile Liability Insurance.
questions.explain: Cyber liability insurance is explicitly designed to protect against losses resulting from data breaches, hacks, or exposure of personally identifiable information (PII) handled by an IT contractor.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: When making the complex decision whether to LEASE or BUY commercial real estate space for an expanding agency department, which of the following strongly points toward LEASING?
options: The department requires extensive, customized structural renovations to accommodate heavy lab equipment.
The program space requirement is temporary, spanning only three years for a specific grant-funded project.
The agency wants to build equity over a 30-year period.
The local commercial real estate prices have severely crashed, making purchase prices historic lows.
questions.explain: Leasing is far more advantageous when the need is temporary. Buying requires a long-term commitment and maintenance, which is inefficient for short-lived, grant-funded programs.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: An agency is deciding how to maintain highly specialized medical diagnostic machines at its public hospital. The two main options are Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) service agreements or Third-Party maintainers. A primary reason to justify an OEM service agreement is:
options: OEM contracts are universally cheaper than third-party options.
OEM mechanics are local city employees.
OEM access to proprietary software updates and specialized parts required for calibration.
OEMs do not require indemnification clauses.
questions.explain: Complex medical equipment often runs on proprietary software. Third-party vendors may lack the legal rights or access to software updates and genuine OEM parts necessary to keep life-saving equipment safely calibrated.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: In a construction solicitation, the buyer establishes a 'Liquidated Damages' clause. To be legally enforceable, liquidated damages must be:
options: Intended to aggressively punish the contractor for failure.
Set to at least triple the estimated actual cost.
A reasonable pre-estimate of the actual financial loss the agency will suffer if the project is delayed.
Kept hidden from the contractor until after a delay occurs.
questions.explain: Liquidated damages are an agreed-upon financial estimate of damages for late delivery. To be enforceable under contract law, they cannot be punitive (a penalty); they must be a reasonable, good-faith estimate of actual anticipated losses.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning
